children: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with representatives of Lockheed Martin
on Monday to discuss accelerating deliveries of Patriot air defense systems as Ukraine struggles to counter Russian missile and drone attacks.
Zelenskyy said in a Telegram post that the discussions focused on expanding supplies of military equipment critical to Ukraine's defenses, including Patriot missile systems and F-16 fighter jets.

The talks highlight the continuing demand for advanced U.S. defense technology as the war in Ukraine strains military inventories. For investors, efforts to increase production and deliveries could support longer-term demand for Lockheed's

fighter jets and missile defense equipment, while also benefiting other contractors involved in the Patriot program. However, the discussions don't necessarily signal new orders or additional revenue.
manufactures the PAC-3 interceptor missiles used by Patriot systems, while RTX
produces the Patriot system and its radar technology. Lockheed
also manufactures the F-16 fighter aircraft operated by Ukraine.

Zelenskyy acknowledged that Ukraine faces significant challenges defending against Russian ballistic missiles and drones. He said the discussions examined opportunities to increase the availability of American-made military equipment.
The meeting comes as Ukraine continues seeking additional Western military support to strengthen its air defenses and protect critical infrastructure from Russian attacks.

title: Zelenskyy seeks faster Patriot missile deliveries from Lockheed Martin
